newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA, NGC move seen simplifying structure.
newsitem.headline: NOVA, NGC move seen simplifying structure.

text.p: A move by NOVA Corp and NGC Corp to split up the assets of their Canadian natural gas partnership, expected to be announced shortly, should simplify the companies' structures and lower costs, analysts said on Wednesday.

Calgary-based NOVA and NGC of Houston confirmed to Reuters late Tuesday they had reached agreement in principle to restructure their ownership in Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd, which operates gas marketing, aggregation and processing and gathering businesses in Canada.
NOVA owns 50.1 percent of Novagas and NGC owns 49.9 percent.

"The way NOVA and NGC Corp control Novagas Clearinghouse, it's just a little complicated, especially as to who really runs this business," said Winifried Fruehauf, analyst with Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion in Toronto.
"(The restructuring) means better lines of communication, operation and administration. I think it's positive."

Under the plan, NOVA would gain full control of Novagas's unregulated gas gathering and processing business as well as its Pan-Alberta Gas aggregator operation, in which it once had 100 percent ownership.
NGC would own Novagas's gas trading and marketing business in a structure that would replicate in Canada its "Energy Store" concept used in the United States.
Major shareholders of NGC, which is currently North America's largest marketer of natural gas, include NOVA, Chevron Corp and British Gas Plc.
Fruehauf said the move would likely have little financial impact on NOVA's and NGC's bottom lines in the near future, although he expected long-term savings.

"There isn't anything immediately that is going to propel what is now Novagas clearinghouse into the stratasphere as a gas marketer or trader," he said. "But over time, I think you're going to see cost reductions and a more efficient organization."
He said the gas processing or "midstream" assets were more aligned to NOVA's traditional business of gas transportation and that NGC's strength was in marketing.

Sam Kanes, analyst with ScotiaMcleod, said that while the move would mean a simpler structure for NOVA, he wondered if a a recent intense level of dissatisfaction with the company among its producer-customers played a role in the decision.
NOVA said on Tuesday that a lawsuit launched against Pan-Alberta by a high-powered group of producers was unrelated to the restructuring of Novagas.
"But going forward, it seems cleaner to have NOVA out of gas marketing and that's what they've agreed to do strategically by making that announcement," Kanes said.

He said the upcoming restructuring announcement was having no impact on NOVA's stock on Wednesday. Investors, who pushed the stock down, were more likely reacting to the lawsuit news, which came to light earlier on Tuesday, he said.
NOVA shares were down 0.10 to 11.65 on volume of 436,000 shares.
